signals.title: Untitled
signals.summary: I wish this weren't phrased as if "AI" were a thing. Americans might be relying more and more on chatbots/LLMs, and imagining that they are a source of information, but calling those systems "AI" I think reinforces the plausiblity of that choice rather than pushing against it.
signals.implication: Track for context; no immediate governance action required.
signals.long_summary: The author expresses concern over the terminology used to describe chatbots and large language models (LLMs) as "AI." They argue that this framing suggests these systems possess a level of reliability and intelligence that may mislead users into viewing them as trustworthy sources of information. Instead of challenging this perception, referring to these technologies as "AI" might inadvertently normalize their use and reliance. This commentary highlights the importance of critically examining language and its impact on public understanding of technology. This matters for a community keeping up with AI, as it encourages a more nuanced discussion about the capabilities and limitations of these systems, promoting informed usage and skepticism.

signals.title: Anthropic launches Cowork, a Claude Desktop agent that works in your files — no coding required
signals.summary: Anthropic released Cowork on Monday, a new AI agent capability that extends the power of its wildly successful Claude Code tool to non-technical users — and according to company insiders, the team built the entire feature in approximately a week and a half, largely using Claude Code itself.
